sections.title: Nationality words
sections.content: The word for a nationality is also the word for its language, without the ending: *magyar* (Hungarian), *angol* (English), *német* (German), *spanyol* (Spanish), *francia* (French). Say who you are with the zero copula you know: *Magyar vagyok.* *Anna spanyol.* No *van* and no article: *Meg angol.* These words are written with a small letter. For more than one person add *-k* after a back vowel with *-ok* and after a front vowel with *-ek*: *angolok, németek*.

sections.title: Asking
sections.content: Ask *Magyar vagy?* (Are you Hungarian?) and answer *Igen, magyar vagyok.* or *Nem, angol vagyok.* The nationality can also come before a noun: *egy angol lány*.
A nationality ends differently from its language: *angol* is the person (and the adjective), *angolul* is how you speak. *Angol vagyok* tells who you are; *angolul beszélek* tells what you speak.
